    class GroupDao(private val database: AppDatabase) {
    
        fun observeGroupsForUser(userId: String): Flow<List<GroupEntity>> =
            database.observeTables(GroupsTable.TABLE_NAME, GroupMembersTable.TABLE_NAME).map {
                withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { getGroupsForUser(userId) }
            }
    
        fun observeAllGroups(): Flow<List<GroupEntity>> =
            database.observeTables(GroupsTable.TABLE_NAME, GroupMembersTable.TABLE_NAME).map {
                withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { getAllGroups() }
            }
    
        fun observeMembersForGroup(groupId: String): Flow<List<GroupMemberEntity>> =
            database.observeTables(GroupMembersTable.TABLE_NAME).map {
                withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { getMembersForGroup(groupId) }
            }
    
        fun upsertGroupWithMembers(group: GroupEntity, members: List<GroupMemberEntity>) {
            val db = database.writableDatabase
            db.beginTransaction()
            try {
                db.insertWithOnConflict(
                    GroupsTable.TABLE_NAME,
                    null,
                    group.toContentValues(),
                    SQLiteDatabase.CONFLICT_REPLACE
                )
                for (member in members) {
                    db.insertWithOnConflict(
                        GroupMembersTable.TABLE_NAME,
                        null,
                        member.toContentValues(),
                        SQLiteDatabase.CONFLICT_REPLACE
                    )
                }
                db.setTransactionSuccessful()
            } finally {
                db.endTransaction()
            }
            database.notifyTableChanged(GroupsTable.TABLE_NAME, GroupMembersTable.TABLE_NAME)
        }
    
        fun upsertGroup(group: GroupEntity) {
            val db = database.writableDatabase
            db.insertWithOnConflict(
                GroupsTable.TABLE_NAME,
                null,
                group.toContentValues(),
                SQLiteDatabase.CONFLICT_REPLACE
            )
            database.notifyTableChanged(GroupsTable.TABLE_NAME)
        }
    
        fun addMember(member: GroupMemberEntity) {
            val db = database.writableDatabase
            db.insertWithOnConflict(
                GroupMembersTable.TABLE_NAME,
                null,
                member.toContentValues(),
                SQLiteDatabase.CONFLICT_REPLACE
            )
            database.notifyTableChanged(GroupMembersTable.TABLE_NAME)
        }
    
        fun removeMember(groupId: String, userId: String) {
            val db = database.writableDatabase
            db.delete(
                GroupMembersTable.TABLE_NAME,
                "${GroupMembersTable.COL_GROUP_ID} = ? AND ${GroupMembersTable.COL_USER_ID} = ?",
                arrayOf(groupId, userId)
            )
            database.notifyTableChanged(GroupMembersTable.TABLE_NAME)
        }
    
        fun deleteGroup(groupId: String) {
            val db = database.writableDatabase
            db.delete(
                GroupsTable.TABLE_NAME,
                "${GroupsTable.COL_ID} = ?",
                arrayOf(groupId)
            )
            database.notifyTableChanged(GroupsTable.TABLE_NAME, GroupMembersTable.TABLE_NAME)
        }
    
        fun getGroupById(groupId: String): GroupEntity? {
            val db = database.readableDatabase
            db.query(
                GroupsTable.TABLE_NAME,
                null,
                "${GroupsTable.COL_ID} = ?",
                arrayOf(groupId),
                null,
                null,
                null
            ).use { cursor ->
                return if (cursor.moveToFirst()) cursor.toGroupEntity() else null
            }
        }
    
        fun getAllGroups(): List<GroupEntity> {
            val db = database.readableDatabase
            val groups = mutableListOf<GroupEntity>()
            db.query(
                GroupsTable.TABLE_NAME,
                null,
                null,
                null,
                null,
                null,
                "${GroupsTable.COL_UPDATED_AT} DESC"
            ).use { cursor ->
                while (cursor.moveToNext()) {
                    groups.add(cursor.toGroupEntity())
                }
            }
            return groups
        }
    
        fun getGroupsForUser(userId: String): List<GroupEntity> {
            val db = database.readableDatabase
            val groups = mutableListOf<GroupEntity>()
            val sql = """
                SELECT g.* FROM ${GroupsTable.TABLE_NAME} g
                INNER JOIN ${GroupMembersTable.TABLE_NAME} gm
                    ON g.${GroupsTable.COL_ID} = gm.${GroupMembersTable.COL_GROUP_ID}
                WHERE gm.${GroupMembersTable.COL_USER_ID} = ?
                ORDER BY g.${GroupsTable.COL_UPDATED_AT} DESC
            """.trimIndent()
            db.rawQuery(sql, arrayOf(userId)).use { cursor ->
                while (cursor.moveToNext()) {
                    groups.add(cursor.toGroupEntity())
                }
            }
            return groups
        }
    
        fun getMembersForGroup(groupId: String): List<GroupMemberEntity> {
            val db = database.readableDatabase
            val members = mutableListOf<GroupMemberEntity>()
            db.query(
                GroupMembersTable.TABLE_NAME,
                null,
                "${GroupMembersTable.COL_GROUP_ID} = ?",
                arrayOf(groupId),
                null,
                null,
                "${GroupMembersTable.COL_JOINED_AT} ASC"
            ).use { cursor ->
                while (cursor.moveToNext()) {
                    members.add(cursor.toGroupMemberEntity())
                }
            }
            return members
        }
    
        fun updateSyncStatus(groupId: String, status: SyncStatus) {
            val db = database.writableDatabase
            val values = ContentValues().apply {
                put(GroupsTable.COL_SYNC_STATUS, Converters.fromSyncStatus(status))
                put(GroupsTable.COL_UPDATED_AT, System.currentTimeMillis())
            }
            db.update(
                GroupsTable.TABLE_NAME,
                values,
                "${GroupsTable.COL_ID} = ?",
                arrayOf(groupId)
            )
            database.notifyTableChanged(GroupsTable.TABLE_NAME)
        }
    
        private fun GroupEntity.toContentValues(): ContentValues = ContentValues().apply {
            put(GroupsTable.COL_ID, id)
            put(GroupsTable.COL_NAME, name)
            put(GroupsTable.COL_DESCRIPTION, description)
            put(GroupsTable.COL_CURRENCY, currency)
            put(GroupsTable.COL_CREATED_BY, createdBy)
            put(GroupsTable.COL_CREATED_AT, createdAt)
            put(GroupsTable.COL_UPDATED_AT, updatedAt)
            put(GroupsTable.COL_SYNC_STATUS, Converters.fromSyncStatus(syncStatus))
        }
    
        private fun GroupMemberEntity.toContentValues(): ContentValues = ContentValues().apply {
            put(GroupMembersTable.COL_GROUP_ID, groupId)
            put(GroupMembersTable.COL_USER_ID, userId)
            put(GroupMembersTable.COL_ROLE, Converters.fromGroupRole(role))
            put(GroupMembersTable.COL_JOINED_AT, joinedAt)
        }
    
        private fun Cursor.toGroupEntity(): GroupEntity {
            val descIdx = getColumnIndexOrThrow(GroupsTable.COL_DESCRIPTION)
            return GroupEntity(
                id = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(GroupsTable.COL_ID)),
                name = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(GroupsTable.COL_NAME)),
                description = if (isNull(descIdx)) null else getString(descIdx),
                currency = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(GroupsTable.COL_CURRENCY)),
                createdBy = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(GroupsTable.COL_CREATED_BY)),
                createdAt = getLong(getColumnIndexOrThrow(GroupsTable.COL_CREATED_AT)),
                updatedAt = getLong(getColumnIndexOrThrow(GroupsTable.COL_UPDATED_AT)),
                syncStatus = Converters.toSyncStatus(getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(GroupsTable.COL_SYNC_STATUS)))
            )
        }
    
        private fun Cursor.toGroupMemberEntity(): GroupMemberEntity = GroupMemberEntity(
            groupId = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(GroupMembersTable.COL_GROUP_ID)),
            userId = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(GroupMembersTable.COL_USER_ID)),
            role = Converters.toGroupRole(getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(GroupMembersTable.COL_ROLE))),
            joinedAt = getLong(getColumnIndexOrThrow(GroupMembersTable.COL_JOINED_AT))
        )
    }

            db.beginTransaction()

                db.insertWithOnConflict(
                    ExpensesTable.TABLE_NAME,
                    null,
                    expense.toContentValues(),
                    SQLiteDatabase.CONFLICT_REPLACE
                )
                db.delete(
                    ExpenseSplitsTable.TABLE_NAME,
                    "${ExpenseSplitsTable.COL_EXPENSE_ID} = ?",
                    arrayOf(expense.id)
                )
                for (split in splits) {
                    db.insertWithOnConflict(
                        ExpenseSplitsTable.TABLE_NAME,
                        null,
                        split.toContentValues(),
                        SQLiteDatabase.CONFLICT_REPLACE
                    )
                }
                db.setTransactionSuccessful()
            } finally {
                db.endTransaction()
            }
            database.notifyTableChanged(ExpensesTable.TABLE_NAME, ExpenseSplitsTable.TABLE_NAME)
        }
    
        fun getExpenseById(expenseId: String): ExpenseEntity? {

            db.query(

                null,

            ).use { cursor ->

        }
    
        fun getSplitsForGroup(groupId: String): List<ExpenseSplitEntity> {

                SELECT s.* FROM ${ExpenseSplitsTable.TABLE_NAME} s
                INNER JOIN ${ExpensesTable.TABLE_NAME} e
                    ON s.${ExpenseSplitsTable.COL_EXPENSE_ID} = e.${ExpensesTable.COL_ID}
                WHERE e.${ExpensesTable.COL_GROUP_ID} = ? AND e.${ExpensesTable.COL_IS_DELETED} = 0
            """.trimIndent()
            db.rawQuery(sql, arrayOf(groupId)).use { cursor ->

            val values = ContentValues().apply {
                put(ExpensesTable.COL_IS_DELETED, 1)
                put(ExpensesTable.COL_SYNC_STATUS, Converters.fromSyncStatus(syncStatus))
            }
            db.update(
                ExpensesTable.TABLE_NAME,
                values,
                "${ExpensesTable.COL_ID} = ?",
                arrayOf(expenseId)
            )
            database.notifyTableChanged(ExpensesTable.TABLE_NAME)
        }
    
        fun updateSyncStatus(expenseId: String, status: SyncStatus) {
            val db = database.writableDatabase
            val values = ContentValues().apply {
                put(ExpensesTable.COL_SYNC_STATUS, Converters.fromSyncStatus(status))
            }
            db.update(
                ExpensesTable.TABLE_NAME,
                values,
                "${ExpensesTable.COL_ID} = ?",
                arrayOf(expenseId)
            )
            database.notifyTableChanged(ExpensesTable.TABLE_NAME)
        }
    
        private fun ExpenseEntity.toContentValues(): ContentValues = ContentValues().apply {
            put(ExpensesTable.COL_ID, id)
            put(ExpensesTable.COL_GROUP_ID, groupId)
            put(ExpensesTable.COL_TITLE, title)
            put(ExpensesTable.COL_AMOUNT_CENTS, amountCents)
            put(ExpensesTable.COL_CURRENCY, currency)
            put(ExpensesTable.COL_PAYER_ID, payerId)
            put(ExpensesTable.COL_CATEGORY, category)
            put(ExpensesTable.COL_NOTES, notes)
            put(ExpensesTable.COL_RECEIPT_LOCAL_URI, receiptLocalUri)
            put(ExpensesTable.COL_RECEIPT_REMOTE_PATH, receiptRemotePath)
            put(ExpensesTable.COL_CREATED_AT, createdAt)
            put(ExpensesTable.COL_CREATED_BY, createdBy)
            put(ExpensesTable.COL_IS_DELETED, if (isDeleted) 1 else 0)
            put(ExpensesTable.COL_SYNC_STATUS, Converters.fromSyncStatus(syncStatus))
        }
    
        private fun ExpenseSplitEntity.toContentValues(): ContentValues = ContentValues().apply {
            put(ExpenseSplitsTable.COL_ID, id)
            put(ExpenseSplitsTable.COL_EXPENSE_ID, expenseId)
            put(ExpenseSplitsTable.COL_USER_ID, userId)
            put(ExpenseSplitsTable.COL_AMOUNT_OWED_CENTS, amountOwedCents)
            put(ExpenseSplitsTable.COL_SHARE_WEIGHT, shareWeight)
        }
    
        private fun Cursor.toExpenseEntity(): ExpenseEntity {
            val notesIdx = getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpensesTable.COL_NOTES)
            val localUriIdx = getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpensesTable.COL_RECEIPT_LOCAL_URI)
            val remotePathIdx = getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpensesTable.COL_RECEIPT_REMOTE_PATH)
            return ExpenseEntity(
                id = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpensesTable.COL_ID)),
                groupId = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpensesTable.COL_GROUP_ID)),
                title = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpensesTable.COL_TITLE)),
                amountCents = getLong(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpensesTable.COL_AMOUNT_CENTS)),
                currency = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpensesTable.COL_CURRENCY)),
                payerId = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpensesTable.COL_PAYER_ID)),
                category = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpensesTable.COL_CATEGORY)),
                notes = if (isNull(notesIdx)) null else getString(notesIdx),
                receiptLocalUri = if (isNull(localUriIdx)) null else getString(localUriIdx),
                receiptRemotePath = if (isNull(remotePathIdx)) null else getString(remotePathIdx),
                createdAt = getLong(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpensesTable.COL_CREATED_AT)),
                createdBy = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpensesTable.COL_CREATED_BY)),
                isDeleted = getInt(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpensesTable.COL_IS_DELETED)) != 0,
                syncStatus = Converters.toSyncStatus(getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpensesTable.COL_SYNC_STATUS)))
            )
        }
    
        private fun Cursor.toExpenseSplitEntity(): ExpenseSplitEntity = ExpenseSplitEntity(
            id = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpenseSplitsTable.COL_ID)),
            expenseId = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpenseSplitsTable.COL_EXPENSE_ID)),
            userId = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpenseSplitsTable.COL_USER_ID)),
            amountOwedCents = getLong(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpenseSplitsTable.COL_AMOUNT_OWED_CENTS)),
            shareWeight = getDouble(getColumnIndexOrThrow(ExpenseSplitsTable.COL_SHARE_WEIGHT))
        )
    }

    class SettlementDao(private val database: AppDatabase) {
    
        fun observeSettlementsForGroup(groupId: String): Flow<List<SettlementEntity>> =
            database.observeTables(SettlementsTable.TABLE_NAME).map {
                withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { getSettlementsForGroup(groupId) }
            }
    
        fun upsertSettlement(settlement: SettlementEntity) {
            val db = database.writableDatabase
            db.insertWithOnConflict(
                SettlementsTable.TABLE_NAME,
                null,
                settlement.toContentValues(),
                SQLiteDatabase.CONFLICT_REPLACE
            )
            database.notifyTableChanged(SettlementsTable.TABLE_NAME)
        }
    
        fun getSettlementsForGroup(groupId: String): List<SettlementEntity> {
            val db = database.readableDatabase
            val settlements = mutableListOf<SettlementEntity>()
            db.query(
                SettlementsTable.TABLE_NAME,
                null,
                "${SettlementsTable.COL_GROUP_ID} = ?",
                arrayOf(groupId),
                null,
                null,
                "${SettlementsTable.COL_CREATED_AT} DESC"
            ).use { cursor ->
                while (cursor.moveToNext()) {
                    settlements.add(cursor.toSettlementEntity())
                }
            }
            return settlements
        }
    
        fun updateSettlementStatus(
            settlementId: String,
            status: SettlementStatus,
            syncStatus: SyncStatus
        ) {
            val db = database.writableDatabase
            val values = ContentValues().apply {
                put(SettlementsTable.COL_STATUS, Converters.fromSettlementStatus(status))
                put(SettlementsTable.COL_SYNC_STATUS, Converters.fromSyncStatus(syncStatus))
            }
            db.update(
                SettlementsTable.TABLE_NAME,
                values,
                "${SettlementsTable.COL_ID} = ?",
                arrayOf(settlementId)
            )
            database.notifyTableChanged(SettlementsTable.TABLE_NAME)
        }
    
        private fun SettlementEntity.toContentValues(): ContentValues = ContentValues().apply {
            put(SettlementsTable.COL_ID, id)
            put(SettlementsTable.COL_GROUP_ID, groupId)
            put(SettlementsTable.COL_DEBTOR_ID, debtorId)
            put(SettlementsTable.COL_CREDITOR_ID, creditorId)
            put(SettlementsTable.COL_AMOUNT_CENTS, amountCents)
            put(SettlementsTable.COL_CURRENCY, currency)
            put(SettlementsTable.COL_PAYMENT_METHOD, paymentMethod)
            put(SettlementsTable.COL_STATUS, Converters.fromSettlementStatus(status))
            put(SettlementsTable.COL_CREATED_AT, createdAt)
            put(SettlementsTable.COL_SYNC_STATUS, Converters.fromSyncStatus(syncStatus))
        }
    
        private fun Cursor.toSettlementEntity(): SettlementEntity = SettlementEntity(
            id = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(SettlementsTable.COL_ID)),
            groupId = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(SettlementsTable.COL_GROUP_ID)),
            debtorId = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(SettlementsTable.COL_DEBTOR_ID)),
            creditorId = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(SettlementsTable.COL_CREDITOR_ID)),
            amountCents = getLong(getColumnIndexOrThrow(SettlementsTable.COL_AMOUNT_CENTS)),
            currency = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(SettlementsTable.COL_CURRENCY)),
            paymentMethod = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(SettlementsTable.COL_PAYMENT_METHOD)),
            status = Converters.toSettlementStatus(getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(SettlementsTable.COL_STATUS))),
            createdAt = getLong(getColumnIndexOrThrow(SettlementsTable.COL_CREATED_AT)),
            syncStatus = Converters.toSyncStatus(getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(SettlementsTable.COL_SYNC_STATUS)))
        )
    }

    class UserDao(private val database: AppDatabase) {
    
        fun observeUserById(userId: String): Flow<UserEntity?> =
            database.observeTables(UsersTable.TABLE_NAME).map {
                withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { getUserById(userId) }
            }
    
        fun observeAllUsers(): Flow<List<UserEntity>> =
            database.observeTables(UsersTable.TABLE_NAME).map {
                withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { getAllUsers() }
            }
    
        fun upsertUser(user: UserEntity) {
            val db = database.writableDatabase
            db.insertWithOnConflict(
                UsersTable.TABLE_NAME,
                null,
                user.toContentValues(),
                SQLiteDatabase.CONFLICT_REPLACE
            )
            database.notifyTableChanged(UsersTable.TABLE_NAME)
        }
    
        fun getUserById(userId: String): UserEntity? {
            val db = database.readableDatabase
            db.query(
                UsersTable.TABLE_NAME,
                null,
                "${UsersTable.COL_ID} = ?",
                arrayOf(userId),
                null,
                null,
                null
            ).use { cursor ->
                return if (cursor.moveToFirst()) cursor.toUserEntity() else null
            }
        }
    
        fun getUserByEmail(email: String): UserEntity? {
            val db = database.readableDatabase
            db.query(
                UsersTable.TABLE_NAME,
                null,
                "${UsersTable.COL_EMAIL} = ?",
                arrayOf(email),
                null,
                null,
                null
            ).use { cursor ->
                return if (cursor.moveToFirst()) cursor.toUserEntity() else null
            }
        }
    
        fun getAllUsers(): List<UserEntity> {
            val db = database.readableDatabase
            val users = mutableListOf<UserEntity>()
            db.query(
                UsersTable.TABLE_NAME,
                null,
                null,
                null,
                null,
                null,
                "${UsersTable.COL_DISPLAY_NAME} ASC"
            ).use { cursor ->
                while (cursor.moveToNext()) {
                    users.add(cursor.toUserEntity())
                }
            }
            return users
        }
    
        fun updateUserCount(userId: String, count: Int, status: SyncStatus) {
            val db = database.writableDatabase
            val values = ContentValues().apply {
                put(UsersTable.COL_COUNT, count)
                put(UsersTable.COL_SYNC_STATUS, Converters.fromSyncStatus(status))
                put(UsersTable.COL_UPDATED_AT, System.currentTimeMillis())
            }
            db.update(
                UsersTable.TABLE_NAME,
                values,
                "${UsersTable.COL_ID} = ?",
                arrayOf(userId)
            )
            database.notifyTableChanged(UsersTable.TABLE_NAME)
        }
    
        fun updateSyncStatus(userId: String, status: SyncStatus) {
            val db = database.writableDatabase
            val values = ContentValues().apply {
                put(UsersTable.COL_SYNC_STATUS, Converters.fromSyncStatus(status))
                put(UsersTable.COL_UPDATED_AT, System.currentTimeMillis())
            }
            db.update(
                UsersTable.TABLE_NAME,
                values,
                "${UsersTable.COL_ID} = ?",
                arrayOf(userId)
            )
            database.notifyTableChanged(UsersTable.TABLE_NAME)
        }
    
        private fun UserEntity.toContentValues(): ContentValues = ContentValues().apply {
            put(UsersTable.COL_ID, id)
            put(UsersTable.COL_EMAIL, email)
            put(UsersTable.COL_DISPLAY_NAME, displayName)
            put(UsersTable.COL_PHOTO_URL, photoUrl)
            put(UsersTable.COL_COUNT, count)
            put(UsersTable.COL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED, if (notificationsEnabled) 1 else 0)
            put(UsersTable.COL_SYNC_STATUS, Converters.fromSyncStatus(syncStatus))
            put(UsersTable.COL_UPDATED_AT, updatedAt)
        }
    
        private fun Cursor.toUserEntity(): UserEntity {
            val photoIdx = getColumnIndexOrThrow(UsersTable.COL_PHOTO_URL)
            val countIdx = getColumnIndex(UsersTable.COL_COUNT)
            return UserEntity(
                id = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(UsersTable.COL_ID)),
                email = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(UsersTable.COL_EMAIL)),
                displayName = getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(UsersTable.COL_DISPLAY_NAME)),
                photoUrl = if (isNull(photoIdx)) null else getString(photoIdx),
                count = if (countIdx >= 0 && !isNull(countIdx)) getInt(countIdx) else 0,
                notificationsEnabled = getInt(getColumnIndexOrThrow(UsersTable.COL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED)) != 0,
                syncStatus = Converters.toSyncStatus(getString(getColumnIndexOrThrow(UsersTable.COL_SYNC_STATUS))),
                updatedAt = getLong(getColumnIndexOrThrow(UsersTable.COL_UPDATED_AT))
            )
        }
    }

    # Database Schema Documentation
    
    This document details the dual-layer database architecture for **"Get Your Money Up Not Your Funny Up"**:
    - **Local Database (Android Room / SQLite)**: Primary offline-first source of truth for the UI, enforcing relational integrity and queueing unsynced operations.
      - Draw.io diagram: [`docs/local_database_schema.drawio.xml`](file:///e:/Documents/GitHub/Mobile-Software-Development-GetYourMoneyUpNotYourFunnyUp/docs/local_database_schema.drawio.xml)
    - **Remote Database (Cloud Firestore)**: Cloud persistence and real-time multi-user synchronization engine.
      - Draw.io diagram: [`docs/remote_database_schema.drawio.xml`](file:///e:/Documents/GitHub/Mobile-Software-Development-GetYourMoneyUpNotYourFunnyUp/docs/remote_database_schema.drawio.xml)
    
    ---
    
    ## 1. Local SQLite / Room Relational Schema
    
    The local database consists of 7 relational tables designed for offline resilience, transactional integrity, and WorkManager synchronization.
    
    ```mermaid
    erDiagram
        users {
            TEXT id PK "Firebase Auth UID or UUID"
            TEXT email "NOT NULL"
            TEXT display_name "NOT NULL"
            TEXT photo_url "NULLABLE"
            INTEGER notifications_enabled "DEFAULT 1"
            TEXT sync_status "SYNCED | PENDING_INSERT | PENDING_UPDATE | PENDING_DELETE | FAILED"
            INTEGER updated_at "Epoch ms"
        }
    
        groups {
            TEXT id PK "UUID"
            TEXT name "NOT NULL"
            TEXT description "NULLABLE"
            TEXT currency "DEFAULT 'EUR'"
            TEXT created_by FK "users.id"
            INTEGER created_at "Epoch ms"
            INTEGER updated_at "Epoch ms"
            TEXT sync_status "Sync state"
        }
    
        group_members {
            TEXT group_id PK,FK "groups.id (ON DELETE CASCADE)"
            TEXT user_id PK,FK "users.id (ON DELETE CASCADE)"
            TEXT role "ADMIN | MEMBER"
            INTEGER joined_at "Epoch ms"
        }
    
        expenses {
            TEXT id PK "UUID"
            TEXT group_id FK "groups.id (ON DELETE CASCADE)"
            TEXT title "NOT NULL"
            INTEGER amount_cents "Minor currency units (Long)"
            TEXT currency "DEFAULT 'EUR'"
            TEXT payer_id FK "users.id"
            TEXT category "DEFAULT 'General'"
            TEXT notes "NULLABLE"
            TEXT receipt_local_uri "NULLABLE"
            TEXT receipt_remote_path "NULLABLE"
            INTEGER created_at "Epoch ms"
            TEXT created_by "users.id"
            INTEGER is_deleted "Soft delete flag (0 or 1)"
            TEXT sync_status "Sync state"
        }
    
        expense_splits {
            TEXT id PK "UUID"
            TEXT expense_id FK "expenses.id (ON DELETE CASCADE)"
            TEXT user_id FK "users.id"
            INTEGER amount_owed_cents "Minor currency units (Long)"
            REAL share_weight "DEFAULT 1.0"
        }
    
        settlements {
            TEXT id PK "UUID"
            TEXT group_id FK "groups.id (ON DELETE CASCADE)"
            TEXT debtor_id FK "users.id"
            TEXT creditor_id FK "users.id"
            INTEGER amount_cents "Minor currency units (Long)"
            TEXT currency "DEFAULT 'EUR'"
            TEXT payment_method "MobilePay | Cash | Bank"
            TEXT status "PENDING | COMPLETED | FAILED"
            INTEGER created_at "Epoch ms"
            TEXT sync_status "Sync state"
        }
    
        sync_queue {
            INTEGER queue_id PK "AUTOINCREMENT"
            TEXT entity_type "USER | GROUP | EXPENSE | SETTLEMENT"
            TEXT entity_id "Target row ID"
            TEXT action "CREATE | UPDATE | DELETE"
            TEXT payload_json "Serialized snapshot"
            INTEGER retry_count "DEFAULT 0"
            INTEGER last_attempt_at "Epoch ms (NULLABLE)"
            TEXT error_message "Last failure reason (NULLABLE)"
        }
    
        users ||--o{ group_members : "joins"
        groups ||--o{ group_members : "has members"
        groups ||--o{ expenses : "contains"
        users ||--o{ expenses : "pays (payer_id)"
        expenses ||--o{ expense_splits : "splits into"
        users ||--o{ expense_splits : "owes (user_id)"
        groups ||--o{ settlements : "tracks"
        users ||--o{ settlements : "pays back (debtor_id)"
        users ||--o{ settlements : "receives (creditor_id)"
    ```
    
    ---
    
    ## 2. Remote Cloud Firestore Document Hierarchy
    
    Firestore uses a hierarchical document-subcollection model under `/groups/{groupId}` so security rules can validate group membership in a single lookup (`request.auth.uid in get(/databases/$(database)/documents/groups/$(groupId)).data.memberIds`).
    
    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
        Root["Firestore Root (/databases/(default)/documents)"]
        UsersCol["Collection: /users/{userId}"]
        GroupsCol["Collection: /groups/{groupId}"]
        ExpensesSub["Subcollection: /groups/{groupId}/expenses/{expenseId}"]
        SettlementsSub["Subcollection: /groups/{groupId}/settlements/{settlementId}"]
    
        Root --> UsersCol
        Root --> GroupsCol
        GroupsCol --> ExpensesSub
        GroupsCol --> SettlementsSub
    
        UsersDoc["User Document
        - id: String
        - email: String
        - displayName: String
        - photoUrl: String?
        - notificationSettings: Map
        - createdAt / updatedAt: Long"]
    
        GroupsDoc["Group Document
        - id: String
        - name: String
        - description: String?
        - currency: String
        - createdBy: String
        - memberIds: List&lt;String&gt;
        - members: List&lt;MemberMap&gt;
        - createdAt / updatedAt: Long"]
    
        ExpensesDoc["Expense Document
        - id: String
        - groupId: String
        - title: String
        - amountCents: Long
        - currency: String
        - payerId: String
        - category: String
        - notes: String?
        - receiptStoragePath: String?
        - splits: List&lt;SplitMap&gt;
        - createdAt: Long
        - createdBy: String
        - isDeleted: Boolean"]
    
        SettlementsDoc["Settlement Document
        - id: String
        - groupId: String
        - debtorId: String
        - creditorId: String
        - amountCents: Long
        - currency: String
        - paymentMethod: String
        - status: String
        - createdAt: Long
        - recordedBy: String"]
    
        UsersCol --- UsersDoc
        GroupsCol --- GroupsDoc
        ExpensesSub --- ExpensesDoc
        SettlementsSub --- SettlementsDoc
    ```
    
    ---
    
    ## 3. Synchronization & Offline-First Data Flow
    
    ```mermaid
    sequenceDiagram
        participant UI as Compose UI / ViewModel
        participant Repo as OfflineFirstRepository
        participant Room as Local Room SQLite DB
        participant WM as WorkManager SyncWorker
        participant FS as Remote Cloud Firestore
    
        UI->>Repo: Create Expense / Settlement
        Repo->>Room: Insert entity (sync_status = PENDING_INSERT) & enqueue sync_queue
        Room-->>UI: Emit updated Flow immediately (non-blocking)
        Repo->>WM: Enqueue OneTimeWorkRequest (NetworkType.CONNECTED)
        WM->>Room: Read pending items from sync_queue
        WM->>FS: Write document to /groups/{groupId}/expenses/{id}
        alt Network Success
            FS-->>WM: ACK
            WM->>Room: Mark entity sync_status = SYNCED & remove from sync_queue
            Room-->>UI: Emit SYNCED status badge
        else Network Failure
            FS-->>WM: Exception / Timeout
            WM->>Room: Increment retry_count & set sync_status = FAILED (or retry backoff)
            Room-->>UI: Emit Pending/Failed indicator
        end
    ```

    /**
     * Defines the relational SQLite schema (tables, columns, foreign keys, and indexes)
     * for the local offline-first database.
     */
    object DatabaseContract {
        const val DATABASE_NAME = "get_your_money_up.db"
        const val DATABASE_VERSION = 2
    
        object UsersTable {
            const val TABLE_NAME = "users"
            const val COL_ID = "id"
            const val COL_EMAIL = "email"
            const val COL_DISPLAY_NAME = "display_name"
            const val COL_PHOTO_URL = "photo_url"
            const val COL_COUNT = "count"
            const val COL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED = "notifications_enabled"
            const val COL_SYNC_STATUS = "sync_status"
            const val COL_UPDATED_AT = "updated_at"
    
            const val CREATE_SQL = """
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS $TABLE_NAME (
                    $COL_ID TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
                    $COL_EMAIL TEXT NOT NULL,
                    $COL_DISPLAY_NAME TEXT NOT NULL,
                    $COL_PHOTO_URL TEXT,
                    $COL_COUNT INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
                    $COL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
                    $COL_SYNC_STATUS TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'SYNCED',
                    $COL_UPDATED_AT INTEGER NOT NULL
                )
            """
        }
    
        object GroupsTable {
            const val TABLE_NAME = "groups"
            const val COL_ID = "id"
            const val COL_NAME = "name"
            const val COL_DESCRIPTION = "description"
            const val COL_CURRENCY = "currency"
            const val COL_CREATED_BY = "created_by"
            const val COL_CREATED_AT = "created_at"
            const val COL_UPDATED_AT = "updated_at"
            const val COL_SYNC_STATUS = "sync_status"
    
            const val CREATE_SQL = """
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS $TABLE_NAME (
                    $COL_ID TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
                    $COL_NAME TEXT NOT NULL,
                    $COL_DESCRIPTION TEXT,
                    $COL_CURRENCY TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'EUR',
                    $COL_CREATED_BY TEXT NOT NULL,
                    $COL_CREATED_AT INTEGER NOT NULL,
                    $COL_UPDATED_AT INTEGER NOT NULL,
                    $COL_SYNC_STATUS TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'SYNCED'
                )
            """
        }
    
        object GroupMembersTable {
            const val TABLE_NAME = "group_members"
            const val COL_GROUP_ID = "group_id"
            const val COL_USER_ID = "user_id"
            const val COL_ROLE = "role"
            const val COL_JOINED_AT = "joined_at"
    
            const val CREATE_SQL = """
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS $TABLE_NAME (
                    $COL_GROUP_ID TEXT NOT NULL,
                    $COL_USER_ID TEXT NOT NULL,
                    $COL_ROLE TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'MEMBER',
                    $COL_JOINED_AT INTEGER NOT NULL,
                    PRIMARY KEY ($COL_GROUP_ID, $COL_USER_ID),
                    FOREIGN KEY ($COL_GROUP_ID) REFERENCES ${GroupsTable.TABLE_NAME}(${GroupsTable.COL_ID}) ON DELETE CASCADE,
                    FOREIGN KEY ($COL_USER_ID) REFERENCES ${UsersTable.TABLE_NAME}(${UsersTable.COL_ID}) ON DELETE CASCADE
                )
            """
        }
    
        object ExpensesTable {
            const val TABLE_NAME = "expenses"
            const val COL_ID = "id"
            const val COL_GROUP_ID = "group_id"
            const val COL_TITLE = "title"
            const val COL_AMOUNT_CENTS = "amount_cents"
            const val COL_CURRENCY = "currency"
            const val COL_PAYER_ID = "payer_id"
            const val COL_CATEGORY = "category"
            const val COL_NOTES = "notes"
            const val COL_RECEIPT_LOCAL_URI = "receipt_local_uri"
            const val COL_RECEIPT_REMOTE_PATH = "receipt_remote_path"
            const val COL_CREATED_AT = "created_at"

    package com.example.getyourmoneyupnotyourfunnyup
    
    import android.os.Bundle
    import androidx.activity.ComponentActivity
    import androidx.activity.compose.setContent
    import androidx.activity.enableEdgeToEdge
    import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxSize
    import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
    import androidx.compose.material3.Scaffold
    import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
    import androidx.compose.runtime.DisposableEffect
    import androidx.compose.runtime.LaunchedEffect
    import androidx.compose.runtime.collectAsState
    import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
    import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
    import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
    import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
    import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
    import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalContext
    import com.example.getyourmoneyupnotyourfunnyup.data.local.AppDatabase
    import com.example.getyourmoneyupnotyourfunnyup.data.repository.AuthRepository
    import com.example.getyourmoneyupnotyourfunnyup.model.User
    import com.example.getyourmoneyupnotyourfunnyup.ui.screens.auth.LoginScreen
    import com.example.getyourmoneyupnotyourfunnyup.ui.screens.auth.RegistrationScreen
    import com.example.getyourmoneyupnotyourfunnyup.ui.screens.counter.CounterScreen
    import com.example.getyourmoneyupnotyourfunnyup.ui.theme.GetYourMoneyUpNotYourFunnyUpTheme
    
    private sealed interface AppDestination {
        data object Login : AppDestination
        data object Register : AppDestination
        data class Counter(val initialUser: User) : AppDestination
    }
    
    class MainActivity : ComponentActivity() {
        override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
            super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
            enableEdgeToEdge()
            setContent {
                GetYourMoneyUpNotYourFunnyUpTheme {
                    Scaffold(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize()) { innerPadding ->
                        AppRoot(
                            modifier = Modifier.padding(innerPadding)
                        )
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    @Composable
    fun AppRoot(modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
        val context = LocalContext.current
        val authRepository = remember {
            val database = AppDatabase.getInstance(context)
            AuthRepository(
                userDao = database.userDao,
                syncQueueDao = database.syncQueueDao
            )
        }
    
        var destination by remember { mutableStateOf<AppDestination>(AppDestination.Login) }
        var displayName by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
        var email by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
        var password by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
        var isLoading by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
        var errorMessage by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }
        var statusMessage by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
    
        // If a session is already active on launch, fetch the user document from Firestore
        LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
            val existingUid = authRepository.currentAuthUid
            val existingEmail = authRepository.currentAuthEmail ?: ""
            if (existingUid != null) {
                isLoading = true
                authRepository.fetchOrCreateUserDocument(
                    uid = existingUid,
                    fallbackEmail = existingEmail,
                    fallbackName = existingEmail.substringBefore("@").ifEmpty { "User" }
                ) { result ->
                    isLoading = false
                    result.onSuccess { user ->
                        statusMessage = "Loaded user from /users/${user.id}"
                        destination = AppDestination.Counter(user)
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    
        when (val current = destination) {
            is AppDestination.Login -> {
                LoginScreen(
                    modifier = modifier,
                    email = email,
                    password = password,
                    isLoading = isLoading,
                    errorMessage = errorMessage,
                    onEmailChange = {
                        email = it
                        errorMessage = null
                    },
                    onPasswordChange = {
                        password = it
                        errorMessage = null
                    },
                    onLoginClick = {
                        isLoading = true
                        errorMessage = null
                        authRepository.loginUser(
                            email = email,
                            password = password
                        ) { result ->
                            isLoading = false
                            result
                                .onSuccess { user ->
                                    statusMessage = "Fetched user from /users/${user.id}"
                                    destination = AppDestination.Counter(user)
                                }
                                .onFailure { err ->
                                    errorMessage = err.localizedMessage ?: "Login failed"
                                }
                        }
                    },
                    onNavigateToRegister = {
                        errorMessage = null
                        destination = AppDestination.Register
                    }
                )
            }
    
            is AppDestination.Register -> {
                RegistrationScreen(
                    modifier = modifier,
                    displayName = displayName,
                    email = email,
                    password = password,
                    isLoading = isLoading,
                    errorMessage = errorMessage,
                    onDisplayNameChange = {
                        displayName = it
                        errorMessage = null
                    },
                    onEmailChange = {
                        email = it
                        errorMessage = null
                    },
                    onPasswordChange = {
                        password = it
                        errorMessage = null
                    },
                    onRegisterClick = {
                        isLoading = true
                        errorMessage = null
                        authRepository.registerUser(
                            displayName = displayName,
                            email = email,
                            password = password
                        ) { result ->
                            isLoading = false
                            result
                                .onSuccess { user ->
                                    statusMessage = "Created user in /users/${user.id}"
                                    destination = AppDestination.Counter(user)
                                }
                                .onFailure { err ->
                                    errorMessage = err.localizedMessage ?: "Registration failed"
                                }
                        }
                    },
                    onNavigateToLogin = {
                        errorMessage = null
                        destination = AppDestination.Login
                    }
                )
            }
    
            is AppDestination.Counter -> {
                val observedUser by authRepository
                    .observeUser(current.initialUser.id)
                    .collectAsState(initial = current.initialUser)
                val activeUser = observedUser ?: current.initialUser
    
                // Attach real-time Firestore listener to `/users/{uid}`
                DisposableEffect(activeUser.id) {
                    val registration = authRepository.listenToUserDocument(
                        uid = activeUser.id,
                        fallbackEmail = activeUser.email,
                        fallbackName = activeUser.displayName,
                        onError = { errMsg ->
                            statusMessage = "Firestore error: $errMsg"
                        }
                    )
                    onDispose {
                        registration.remove()
                    }
                }
    
                CounterScreen(
                    modifier = modifier,
                    user = activeUser,
                    statusMessage = statusMessage,
                    onIncrementClick = {
                        statusMessage = "Saving count to /users/${activeUser.id}..."
                        authRepository.incrementUserCount(activeUser) { result ->
                            result
                                .onSuccess { savedCount ->
                                    statusMessage = "Saved count ($savedCount) to /users/${activeUser.id}"
                                }
                                .onFailure { err ->
                                    statusMessage = "Offline / Failed: ${err.localizedMessage}"
                                }
                        }
                    },
                    onLogoutClick = {
                        authRepository.signOut()
                        password = ""
                        errorMessage = null
                        statusMessage = ""
                        destination = AppDestination.Login
                    }
                )
            }
        }
    }

    DOCUMENT: Documentation\Android Project Overview.pdf PAGES: 3
    PAGE 1 TERMS background
    
    
    
    
    Objective
    Develop a mobile application (Android) that helps groups of people track and manage their shared
    expenses, ensuring everyone is aware of their financial obligations with a friendly and intuitive user
    interface. If you�re familiar with the application WeShare or groups in MobilePay, the concept is very
    much the same.
    Background
    In various social and formal gatherings, expenses often occur that are typically shared among
    participants, such as meals, gifts, or travel costs. Tracking who paid what and calculating how much
    others owe can become a cumbersome task. A mobile application that alleviates this burden by
    calculating and notifying members of their respective dues can be incredibly beneficial.
    Functional Requirements
    User Registration & Profile Management:
    �
    Allow users to create a profile, including essential information like name and contact details.
    �
    Enable users to update their profiles and manage notification settings.
    �
    You can manage users by creating a custom authentication system, using a third-party provider
    such as Firebase Authentication or by using dummy data and mocking interactions. (Database
    and security is not required, but is recommended)
    Group Management:
    �
    Allow the creation of groups, adding and removing participants.
    �
    Permit the naming and description of the group.
    Expense Entry & Management:
    �
    Enable users to input expenses, specifying the payer and the amount.
    �
    Allow attachment of receipts or invoices (optional feature).
    �
    Facilitate the splitting of expenses among all or selected group members.
    Debt Calculation:
    �
    Implement algorithms to calculate how much each person owes or is owed in a group.
    �
    Allow users to view a summary of all transactions, and their current balance (owed/owing)
    within a group.
    Notifications & Communications:
    �
    Notify group members of new expenses and updates.
    �
    Allow users to send reminder notifications to those who owe them money.
    
    
    PAGE 2 TERMS offline,reliab,repository,background
    
    
    
    
    Non-functional Requirements
    Reliability (Quality Attribute, QA):
    �
    Fault Tolerance
    o If a request fails due to temporary network unavailability, the application must retry it in
    the background
    o Failed requests must not prevent the user from continuing to use the app
    �
    Offline Availability
    o Previously retrieved data must remain accessible when the device is offline
    �
    User feedback
    o The application must indicate whether a request is pending, successful or failed
    o The user must be notified when a previously failed request eventually succeeds in the
    background
    Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence:
    GenAI has become a well-established tool for software development and therefore its use is accepted.
    As engineers we must know when and how to use such tools therefore we expect you to state an
    example of the following for each of your GenAI use-cases:
    Use case: (e.g. UX, code-completion, library integration):
    Tool: (e.g. gemini, chatGPT, Claude)
    Chat history: (link if possible)
    Evaluation: (Description of how well the LLM carried out its task and to what extent you could use its
    replies)
    Look up alternative solutions yourselves (not using GenAI) - why did you end up using what solution?
    
    AI policy (shared constant)
    Allowed: any AI tool in any mode, autocomplete, chat, multimodal, or agentic (e.g., Claude Code,
    Cursor, GitHub Copilot agent mode, Gemini CLI), for any part of this project, provided use is disclosed.
    Undisclosed AI use is academic misconduct. Note the asymmetry: controlled disclosed AI use that is
    verified well can earn top marks; hidden use can cost you the course.
    Four standing rules apply whenever AI touches your project:
    1. Disclose in the AI dossier. Continue the log you started in the design document's Appendix A: one
    entry per significant interaction (tool, mode, task, prompt or link, verification, decision), plus the
    failure log, at least 3 entries per project documenting AI output that was wrong or off-spec and how
    you caught it.
    2. AI code enters main only through a pull request that carries tests, is reviewed by a teammate who
    did not generate it, and passes CI. 'The model wrote it and it ran' is not verification.
    3. Maintain an agent rules file. Your repository contains a CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md describing your
    conventions, architecture, and definition of done. Evolve it as you learn what your agents get wrong;
    its git history is evidence of engineering judgment.

    MVVM
    • Pattern that separates responsibilities into three layers:
    • View
    • ViewModel
    • Model
    • View
    • Displays the UI
    • Receives user input
    • Contains minimal business logic
    • ViewModel
    • Holds UI state
    • Contains presentation logic
    • Survives configuration changes
    • Model
    • Data and business logic
    • Database
    • Repository
    • This and other architectures are described in a later lecture
    
    PAGE 15 TERMS viewmodel
    ViewModel - Benefits
    • Prevents data loss
    during configuration changes.
    • Reduces boilerplate code.
    • Promotes a cleaner architecture
    by separating data from UI.
    Source
    Further reading:ViewModel
    
    PAGE 16 TERMS viewmodel
    Creating ViewModels
    • ViewModel for displaying a name
    • _name is mutable and private
    • MutableStateFlow holds a value that
    can be changed, and sends new value
    to observers
    • name is read-only and public
    • asStateFlow() creates read-only copy
    • _name can only be changed using the
    public function setName()
    
    PAGE 17 TERMS viewmodel
    Using ViewModels
    • ViewModel is passed to the screen that uses it
    • = viewModel() means that an instance is created if one is not passed
    • If multiple screens use the same VM, the same instance should be
    passed between them
    • collectAsStateWithLifeCycle() observes a StateFlow and converts it
    to Compose State
    • In this example, it
    becomes a String that
    can be displayed in
    the UI
    
    PAGE 22 TERMS viewmodel
    State Management with ViewModels
    • Centralized state management
    ViewModels hold and manage state
    in one place
    • Shareable across composables
    Pass ViewModels from parent to
    child for shared state
    • Survives configuration changes -
    State persists across rotations and
    recreations
    • Separation of concerns - Business
    logic stays in ViewModel, UI logic in
    composables
    Further reading:ViewModel
    
    PAGE 23 TERMS viewmodel,background
    Why ViewModels over remember(Saveable?)
    When to use ViewModels
    • Complex business logic
    • State shared across multiple screens
    • Background operations (Networks calls)
    • State that needs to survive process death
    When remember(Saveable) is enough
    • Simple UI state (toggle, text input)
    • State only used within a single composable
    • No business logic involved
    • Primitive types only
    The problem with remember(Saveable) everywhere
    • Prop drilling nightmare
    • No separation between UI and potential business logic
    • Awkward for complex objects
    • No lifecycle-aware coroutine scope
    Further reading:ViewModel

    Exercise – Use ViewModel instead of

    • Design and create a viewmodel that is able to externalize the

    PAGE 7 TERMS background
    Background
    usability and software architecture
    Scenario-based architecture-level usability analysis
    Folmer et al.: evaluate usability explicitly during architectural
    design, to find usability issues early.
    Walk a usability scenario (“user cancels a long upload”) through the
    architecture and see which components must change.
    Usability scenarios → design patterns
    Bass et al.: a catalogue of usability scenarios, each paired with
    a high-level pattern that supports it.
    The scenario–pattern pairs expose the cross-relationships between
    usability and architecture; they also help when drawing use cases,
    class and sequence diagrams.
    usability scenario
    responsibilities
    components and
    connectors
    cost and test
    Same move as last week: a scenario in, a design decision out. The only difference is the quality attribute.
    7
    
    PAGE 8 TERMS background
    Background
    why mobile is different
    Motion
    people walk, ride, drive;
    test in the lab and in the
    field
    Context and location
    results depend on where
    the user is and what else
    is happening
    Physical and mental
    demands
    one hand, sunlight, noise,
    interruptions, small
    screen
    Hardware limits
    battery, radio, GPS that
    fails indoors
    Multimodal
    interaction
    speech, vibration, sound,
    location-aware services
    Mobile A/B testing helps with
    •
    avoiding platform-specific frustration
    •
    simple navigation
    •
    clear content
    •
    fewer steps
    But A/B tests improve the UI, not the mechanism
    We also need to know whether a mechanism works (does the
    progress bar reduce uncertainty? does vibration beat sound on a
    street?) and what it does to the architecture.
    Your study design sessions covered the first half; today is the second half: the mechanism and its cost.

    The seven, in your expense app
    and where each one lives in last week’s diagram
    Mechanism
    In the expense app
    Lives in
    System status feedback
    pending / synced / failed badge on an expense; “offline” chip
    sync state in Room, mapped by the ViewModel, rendered by the
    screen
    System progress feedback
    receipt upload: bar with percent and remaining time
    WorkManager setProgress, collected by the ViewModel
    Abort
    cancel an upload; leave group with confirmation
    WorkManager cancelUniqueWork; a confirm dialog
    Long action feedback
    “Syncing 3 changes…” while the outbox drains
    outbox row count exposed as state
    Interaction
    short vibration when a reminder is sent; sound off by default
    Vibrator service, called from the worker on success
    Warning
    “You are offline: changes will sync later”; “Delete this expense?”
    connectivity callback; dialog before destructive actions
    Retry
    “Tap to retry” on a failed expense after the last automatic attempt
    re-enqueue the outbox row; worker
    Each row is a responsibility, and a responsibility belongs to a component. That is what makes usability an architecture
    topic.

    RQ3: what the users said
    one line per mechanism
    Mechanism
    Result
    Takeaway for your app
    System status feedback
    44% high satisfaction, 48% medium, 8% low; most found the messages
    sufficient
    a status badge and a short message are enough; do not over-
    explain
    Long action feedback
    68% found the timer adequate, 24% not, 8% no answer
    show time or progress for anything over a few seconds
    Abort
    32% immediate, 68% quick, nobody slow; three asked for a cancellation
    message
    cancel must answer at once, and say that it cancelled
    Interaction
    all satisfied with vibration; 68% adequate in noise, 28% disagreed
    vibration beats sound outdoors; keep it short
    Warning + SSF
    48% felt there were too many mechanisms; 19 preferred visual, 13
    vibration, nobody chose sound
    combine at most two channels; never rely on sound
    Retry
    GPS accurate; everyone wanted the retry option within 5 minutes at most
    offer manual retry early; do not make the user wait for backoff
    Progress feedback
    useful for all; speed judged correct; no improvements suggested
    a determinate bar, when you can compute one, is the safest
    mechanism of the seven

    Summary
    Usability is architectural
    the seven mechanisms are
    responsibilities with owners: feedback,
    progress, abort, long actions, interaction,
    warning, retry. Level 1 is colours; levels 2
    and 3 are classes.
    It is affordable
    about ten percent of code in the case
    study, no change of style, a few new
    relationships; the cost grows when
    mechanisms cooperate, so choose few.
    Test it where the user is
    nobody chose sound on the street; half
    felt three channels were too many; cancel
    must be immediate and say so; retry
    within minutes.
    For the report  the three-mechanism table from today sits next to last week’s reliability scenario: the feedback bullet of the brief is answered by
    naming the mechanism, its owner and its test.
    Reading: Capilla, Kazman, Romera and Carrillo, “Usability implications in software architecture: the case study of a
    mobile app”, Software: Practice and Experience, 2020.

    PAGE 4 TERMS room,repository
    Architecture versus its representation
    Every software system has an architecture. It may, however, not be known to anyone. So there is a difference between the
    architecture and the representation of it.
    Architecture
    reality embedded in the system
    •
    the Kotlin code as it actually is, in the repository
    •
    the coroutines and flows that actually run on the phone
    •
    the Room file on the device, the backend it actually talks
    to
    •
    your app already has one, even if it is “everything in
    MainActivity”
    Architecture representation
    our description of it
    •
    in documents, in our collective minds, on napkins, in
    whiteboard photos
    •
    the diagram and the component descriptions in your
    implementation document
    •
    always partial: a representation picks a view and leaves
    the rest out
    •
    can be wrong: the diagram says MVVM, the code calls
    Room from a composable
    Your report is the representation; the examiner also opens the repository, which is the architecture. Make the two
    agree before 24 November.
    4
    
    PAGE 5 TERMS reliab,sync,repository,viewmodel
    Why spend time on architecture? Four jobs it does
    An investment
    We invest in it to reduce the cost of producing the software
    later; so the investment must be sensible.
    In your app: an hour deciding that all network calls go through one
    repository, saves a day of hunting duplicated retry code the week
    before the deadline.
    An abstraction
    Omit detail to cope with complexity: a common overview, a
    common goal, compact documentation, and perhaps reuse.
    In your app: “UI, ViewModel, repository, worker, backend” is five
    boxes; the code is five thousand lines. The five boxes are what
    the team can hold in its head.
    A means of communication
    Understanding, discussion and consensus between all
    stakeholders, technical and not.
    In your app: the one diagram that lets the person writing the sync
    worker and the person writing the screen agree on who shows the
    “pending” state.
    A design plan
    Early analysis, risk assessment, balancing qualities against
    each other; the bridge between requirements and
    implementation.
    In your app: deciding now that writes are local-first fixes both the

    Views: one system, several structures
    “A view represents a partial aspect of a software
    architecture that shows specific properties of a
    software system.”
    Buschmann et al., Pattern-Oriented Software Architecture
    Consider a bridge
    The structural engineer sees joints and forces (sum of
    forces at joint 2 equals zero). The architect sees shape and
    proportion. The electrician sees the cable runs. The driver
    sees a road. Same bridge, four drawings, none of them
    wrong, none of them complete.
    The same expense app, seen three ways
    Module view: the code at rest
    packages ui, viewmodel, domain, data; classes and interfaces; who depends
    on whom
    what you see in Android Studio’s project tree
    Component and connector view: the code running
    a GroupViewModel instance, a StateFlow, a coroutine in viewModelScope, a
    WorkManager job, an HTTPS session
    what you see in the profiler and the logcat
    Allocation view: the code placed
    the APK in an app process on the phone, the Room file in app storage, the
    API on a server, the push service
    what you see when you deploy
    “We cannot communicate meaningfully about software unless it is clear which structure we are describing.” Bass et al.
    So label every diagram with its view.

    Elements of an architectural description
    Architectural views (N)
    What is the software architecture?
    •
    Module viewpoint - static: packages, classes, interfaces
    •
    Component and connector viewpoint - dynamic:
    processes, objects, executing stuff
    •
    Allocation viewpoint - physical: devices, networks,
    servers
    Multiple viewpoints exist (Kruchten’s 4+1, Clements’ Views and
    Beyond); we use these three.
    Architectural requirements (+1)
    Why is the software architecture the way it is?
    •
    Scenario-based requirements - paths through the
    significant use cases: add an expense while the train is in
    a tunnel
    •
    Quality-attribute requirements - the primary concerns,
    written as quality attribute specifications: your reliability
    QA
    •
    Design decisions - and the reasons: “local-first, because
    the QA says the user must continue using the app”
    The views answer “what”; the +1 answers “why”. A report with only views is a drawing; a report with both is an
    argument.

    The contribution of Bass, Clements and Kazman
    A quality framework
    Three families of qualities: system
    qualities (availability, performance, …),

    The quality attribute scenario (QAS): the

    slide 18
    Quality anchored in context
    No quality is globally achievable. A
    scenario says who, under which

    A writing template: the quality attribute scenario
    Six parts, always in this order; the same for every quality
    Source
    Stimulus
    Environment
    Artifact
    Response
    Response measure
    Source of stimulus
    Some entity (a human, a computer system,
    any other actuator) that generated the
    stimulus.
    e.g. a group member; the backend; the OS; a
    timer
    Stimulus
    A condition that needs to be considered
    when it arrives at the system.
    e.g. adds an expense; the network drops; 1,000
    expenses arrive; a permission is revoked
    Environment
    The conditions under which the stimulus
    occurs: normal operation, overload,
    degraded mode, …
    e.g. foreground use; brief outage; low battery;
    metered network
    Artifact
    The part that is stimulated: the whole
    system or some piece of it.
    e.g. ExpenseRepository and SyncWorker;
    GroupScreen; the Room database
    Response
    The activity undertaken after the arrival of
    the stimulus.
    e.g. write locally, show pending, enqueue, retry,
    notify
    Response measure
    How the response is measured, so that the
    requirement can be tested.
    e.g. delivered within 60 s of reconnect; UI thread
    never blocked; 100 percent of queued requests
    delivered
    If you cannot write the response measure, you do not have a requirement yet; you have a hope. The measure is what the test
    asserts.

    From the brief to the scenario
    •
    “provide contextual feedback on successful and failed transactions” → the response’s first clause, measured by the 100 ms and 5 s numbers
    •
    “retry in the background without affecting the user’s continued usage” → the response’s second and third clauses, measured by “UI thread never
    blocked”
    •
    “time between retries with decreasing frequency” → the backoff series in the measure; WorkManager’s exponential policy gives it for free
    •
    “user gets notified when the request has finally been completed” → the notification clause and its 5-second measure

    What a tactic is
    Stimulus
    a request fails
    Tactics to control the response
    retry with backoff, outbox, local-first writes…
    Response
    delivered later, user told
    Tactic
    a design decision that influences the control of a quality
    attribute response
    e.g. a heartbeat to control availability; exponential backoff to
    control availability and energy
    Architectural strategy
    a collection of tactics; your reliability strategy is five tactics
    working together
    Characteristics
    •
    they capture what architects do in practice: a catalogue of known
    moves, not inventions
    •
    tactics may refine other tactics: “retry” refines “recover”;
    “exponential backoff” refines “retry”
    •
    tactics may influence more than one quality attribute, since
    qualities are interdependent: backoff helps availability and energy,
    costs latency
    •
    a tactic is not a pattern: a pattern (MVVM, repository) packages
    several tactics and their trade-offs
    A tactic modifies the response measure for a given stimulus. If you cannot say which number it moves, it is not a
    tactic, it is a feature.

    Energy efficiency tactics
    Kjærgaard and Kuhrmann, QoSA 2015: tactics for sensing, energy awareness, processing and sharing
    In your expense app
    •
    Event-based processing: sync when an expense is
    added, not on a timer; the outbox makes this natural
    •
    Demand-driven sharing: the backend pushes
    changes (FCM); the phone does not poll
    •
    Communication selection: receipts only over
    unmetered Wi-Fi; expenses over anything
    •

    the backoff and skip image uploads
    •
    Dynamic duty cycle: exponential backoff is a duty
    cycle that stretches while the network is absent
    •
    Not for you: sensor selection and replacement
    belong to sensing apps
    Each retry wakes the radio, which costs more than the request itself. Backoff is an energy tactic as much as an
    availability one.

    Resource adaptability tactics
    Kjærgaard and Kuhrmann, QoSA 2015: tactics for resource availability, processing and quality awareness
    In your expense app
    •
    Resource selection: prefer Wi-Fi for large payloads;
    the OS picks the network, you pick the constraint
    •
    Mask variability: the outbox and the local-first write
    hide the outage from the user; the stimulus “network
    disappears” never reaches the screen as an error
    •
    Resource prediction: a connectivity callback tells
    you the network is gone before the request fails; stop
    enqueueing network work and show offline mode
    •
    Application adaptation: degrade on purpose: on
    metered links sync expenses, defer receipts; on no
    link, read and write locally
    •
    Increase resources: not available on a phone; you
    adapt instead
    Mask variability is the tactic that your whole reliability design is: the user keeps working as if the network were there.

     Architecture versus its representation
    Every software system has an architecture. It may, however, not be known to anyone. So there is a difference between the
    architecture and the representation of it.
    Architecture
    reality embedded in the system
    •
    the Kotlin code as it actually is, in the repository
    •
    the coroutines and flows that actually run on the phone
    •
    the Room file on the device, the backend it actually talks
    to
    •
    your app already has one, even if it is “everything in
    MainActivity”
    Architecture representation
    our description of it
    •
    in documents, in our collective minds, on napkins, in
    whiteboard photos
    •
    the diagram and the component descriptions in your
    implementation document
    •
    always partial: a representation picks a view and leaves
    the rest out
    •
    can be wrong: the diagram says MVVM, the code calls
    Room from a composable
    Your report is the representation; the examiner also opens the repository, which is the architecture. Make the two
    agree before 24 November.
    4
    
    
    DOCUMENT Documentation/Lectures/Software Architecture Part 1.pdf PAGE 5
     Why spend time on architecture? Four jobs it does
    An investment
    We invest in it to reduce the cost of producing the software
    later; so the investment must be sensible.
    In your app: an hour deciding that all network calls go through one
    repository, saves a day of hunting duplicated retry code the week
    before the deadline.
    An abstraction
    Omit detail to cope with complexity: a common overview, a
    common goal, compact documentation, and perhaps reuse.
    In your app: “UI, ViewModel, repository, worker, backend” is five
    boxes; the code is five thousand lines. The five boxes are what
    the team can hold in its head.
    A means of communication
    Understanding, discussion and consensus between all
    stakeholders, technical and not.
    In your app: the one diagram that lets the person writing the sync
    worker and the person writing the screen agree on who shows the
    “pending” state.
    A design plan
    Early analysis, risk assessment, balancing qualities against
    each other; the bridge between requirements and
    implementation.
    In your app: deciding now that writes are local-first fixes both the
    reliability QA and the architecture of every screen that shows a
    balance.
    “Architecture gives us intellectual control over the very complex by allowing us to substitute the complex with a set of interacting pieces, each
    one of which is substantially simpler than the whole.”
    5
    
    
    DOCUMENT Documentation/Lectures/Software Architecture Part 1.pdf PAGE 6
     Views: one system, several structures
    “A view represents a partial aspect of a software
    architecture that shows specific properties of a
    software system.”
    Buschmann et al., Pattern-Oriented Software Architecture
    Consider a bridge
    The structural engineer sees joints and forces (sum of
    forces at joint 2 equals zero). The architect sees shape and
    proportion. The electrician sees the cable runs. The driver
    sees a road. Same bridge, four drawings, none of them
    wrong, none of them complete.
    The same expense app, seen three ways
    Module view: the code at rest
    packages ui, viewmodel, domain, data; classes and interfaces; who depends
    on whom
    what you see in Android Studio’s project tree
    Component and connector view: the code running
    a GroupViewModel instance, a StateFlow, a coroutine in viewModelScope, a
    WorkManager job, an HTTPS session
    what you see in the profiler and the logcat
    Allocation view: the code placed
    the APK in an app process on the phone, the Room file in app storage, the
    API on a server, the push service
    what you see when you deploy
    “We cannot communicate meaningfully about software unless it is clear which structure we are describing.” Bass et al.
    So label every diagram with its view.
    6

     Elements of an architectural description
    Architectural views (N)
    What is the software architecture?
    •
    Module viewpoint - static: packages, classes, interfaces
    •
    Component and connector viewpoint - dynamic:
    processes, objects, executing stuff
    •
    Allocation viewpoint - physical: devices, networks,
    servers
    Multiple viewpoints exist (Kruchten’s 4+1, Clements’ Views and
    Beyond); we use these three.
    Architectural requirements (+1)
    Why is the software architecture the way it is?
    •
    Scenario-based requirements - paths through the
    significant use cases: add an expense while the train is in
    a tunnel
    •
    Quality-attribute requirements - the primary concerns,
    written as quality attribute specifications: your reliability
    QA
    •
    Design decisions - and the reasons: “local-first, because
    the QA says the user must continue using the app”
    The views answer “what”; the +1 answers “why”. A report with only views is a drawing; a report with both is an
    argument.

     Module viewpoint
    Elements: classes, packages, interfaces.  Relations: associations, generalizations, realizations, dependencies.  UML: class and package diagrams.
    What it answers
    •
    how the code is divided and who may depend on
    whom
    •
    where a change lands: adding “attach receipt”
    touches ui, domain and data, but not viewmodel’s
    balance logic
    •
    what can be tested in isolation: domain has no
    Android imports, so DebtCalculator runs as a plain
    JVM unit test
    •
    which direction dependencies point: downwards
    only, so the UI never imports Room
    In the report
    a package diagram with the dependency arrows, and one
    line per package saying what it owns

    GroupScreen, AddExpenseScreen,
    composables, navigation

    GroupViewModel, ExpenseViewModel,
    UiState
    domain
    Expense, Group, Member,
    DebtCalculator
    data
    ExpenseRepository, ExpenseDao (Room),
    RemoteApi, Outbox, SyncWorker
    dashed arrow = depends on (imports)
    Domain knows nothing about Android; data knows Room and the network;
    viewmodel knows domain and data; ui knows viewmodel. Dependencies point

     Component and connector viewpoint
    Elements: components with functional behaviour.  Relations: connectors for control and communication.  UML: object and interaction diagrams.
    Components
    what part of the running system is doing what: a
    ViewModel instance, a repository, a worker, the backend
    Connectors
    how they talk: a StateFlow, a suspend call, SQL through
    a DAO, HTTPS with JSON, a push message. A
    connector defines the protocol, the ordering of
    operations, and the roles of the attached components.
    Mapping to UML
    components are active objects; connectors are links with
    messages; add a textual description of responsibilities

     Why the C&C view is central, and two caveats
    What earns money in a software
    company?
    Class diagrams and text files of Kotlin
    classes? Or executing objects doing what
    the user wants? The running system is
    what the user pays for and what the brief
    tests; the C&C view is the one that
    describes it.
    Moral: this is a central viewpoint.
    Caveat 1: C&C does not map well
    to code
    Few languages have interaction as a
    first-class construct; a “connector”
    becomes a StateFlow, a suspend call, an
    HTTP client, an intent. So the diagram
    and the code drift apart unless you keep
    them together on purpose.
    In the report: name the Kotlin construct
    behind every connector.
    Caveat 2: UML was not designed
    for architecture
    Many of its constructs are irrelevant here,
    and it has no connector concept; but it is
    widely known and supported, and the
    examiner can read it.
    In the report: UML where it helps, boxes
    and labelled arrows where it does not;
    always a legend.

     Your architecture diagram for the report
    One page, one argument: this is how the design meets the reliability QA
    Do
    •
    say which view it is (usually component and connector, with
    the allocation boundary drawn as a dashed line around the
    phone)
    •
    name every element with the real class or module name
    from your repository
    •
    label every connector with its construct: StateFlow, suspend
    call, Room DAO, WorkManager, HTTPS
    •
    mark where the reliability tactics live: outbox, worker with
    backoff, feedback state in the ViewModel, notification
    •
    add a legend and a short paragraph: stimulus, response,
    which component responds, how you tested it
    Common mistakes
    •
    a diagram of the screens: that is the navigation model from
    the design document, not an architecture
    •
    boxes without arrows, or arrows without labels
    •
    a cloud called “Backend” and a box called “App”, nothing in
    between
    •
    a textbook MVVM picture that does not contain the words
    outbox, retry or backoff although the QA is reliability
    •
    a diagram that disagrees with the code; the examiner opens
    the repository

     Part 3
    Quality attributes
    A way to express architectural requirements. “Reliable” is an opinion; a scenario with a response measure
    is a requirement you can test, and the brief asks you to test it.
    13
    
    
    DOCUMENT Documentation/Lectures/Software Architecture Part 1.pdf PAGE 14
     No such thing as “good” or “bad”
    We are engineers and scientists, not priests: the problem with good and bad is that they are subjective. We need to measure.
    Quality attribute
    the aspect we care about:
    performance, reliability, energy,
    privacy
    Metric
    the scale we agree on:
    milliseconds, percent of
    requests, mAh per hour
    Measurement
    the number we actually get, on
    a real phone, under stated
    conditions
    Choose between
    alternatives
    outbox and worker, or retry loop
    in the ViewModel? The
    numbers decide
    Quality attribute
    A metric you can actually collect on Android
    How you would collect it
    Performance
    time to first frame of GroupScreen; dropped frames while scrolling
    Macrobenchmark or a stopwatch in a Compose UI test;
    the profiler’s jank view
    Reliability
    share of queued requests delivered after an outage; time from
    reconnect to delivery; crash-free sessions
    an instrumented test with airplane mode; Firebase
    Crashlytics or Play Vitals
    Energy efficiency
    battery percent per hour of typical use; wake-ups per hour
    Battery Historian, Android Studio energy profiler
    Usability
    task success rate, time on task, System Usability Scale score
    the study design you did in sessions 8 and 9
    A quality attribute without a metric is a wish. A metric without a measurement is a plan. The report wants
    measurements.
